Education and training; infrastructure; labour market reforms; lower direct taxes; deregulation; incentives to invest; privatisation.

Total output ÷ number of workers (per period).

front: How can supply-side policy reduce inflation?
back: It raises capacity and lowers unit costs, so output can grow without demand exceeding supply.

front: Which type of unemployment does training tackle best?
back: Structural unemployment, caused by a mismatch of skills.

front: Give three limitations of supply-side policy.
back: Long time lags; high cost; uncertain responses to incentives; may increase inequality; privatisation can create private monopolies.
